title: How Hate Speech Varies by Target Identity: A Computational Analysis
base_benchmarks: Social Bias Inference Corpus (Sap et al., 2020)
findings: The study found that hate speech varies significantly based on the target's demographic category, with religion being a key dimension of this variation. Classifiers trained on hate speech targeting religious identities performed poorly when generalizing to other categories like gender/sexuality. The language of hate speech was found to be specific to the targeted religious group, employing distinct vocabularies (e.g., 'holocaust', 'gas', 'oven' for Jews; 'terrorist', 'bomb' for Muslims; 'priest', 'catholic' for Christians). There was some overlap in classifier generalization between hate targeting religious groups and racial/ethnic groups, which the authors suggest may be due to the frequent conflation of these identities (e.g., viewing Jewish identity as both religious and racial, or conflating Muslims and Arabs).

measurement_description: Hate speech classifier generalization across different religious target groups. The study measured how well a classifier trained on hate speech directed at one religious group (e.g., Christians) could detect hate speech directed at other religious groups (e.g., Jews, Muslims).
